ENT CLINICAL NOTE  

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: No ENT‐related presenting complaint. Consultation was for dysuria; no ENT trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: No throat, nasal, otologic, or neck symptoms reported at any time during current illness.
- ENT symptoms:  
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denied  
  • Drooling: Denied  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Denied  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Denied  
  • Dyspnea: Denied  
  • Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): Denied currently; history of swelling with clindamycin exposure (see allergies)  
  • Ear pain/hearing change: Denied  
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denied
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No previous ENT emergencies or airway compromise reported. No prior adrenaline/epinephrine use.
- Allergies and current medications:  
  • Drug allergy – Clindamycin: causes swelling (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  • Current medications: None regular. Attempted over-the-counter sodium bicarbonate for dysuria (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context: 19-year-old college student living with friends; no supervision concerns noted.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not observed/reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or increased work of breathing reported.
- Mental status: Alert and oriented; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient: Not applicable during teleconsultation.

Assessment:
- No active ENT pathology identified.  
- History of drug-induced swelling (clindamycin) – consistent with probable IgE-mediated or non-IgE drug hypersensitivity; currently asymptomatic from an ENT standpoint.

Plan:
- Drug allergy education: advised strict avoidance of clindamycin; document allergy with all healthcare providers.  
- Emergency precautions: patient instructed to seek immediate medical attention/call emergency services if future exposure leads to throat swelling, voice change, dyspnea, or facial/oral swelling.  
- No ENT interventions required at this time.  
- Routine follow-up: none needed for ENT unless allergic manifestations recur.  
- Provided red-flag education: breathing difficulty, throat tightness, drooling, stridor, voice change, or rapid facial/oral swelling → call emergency number (e.g., 911) immediately.
